analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bremen host the bottom side five days after the Nordderby. The brief lists Ko Itakura as missing, but his yellow-red ban is a one-match suspension to be served against Dortmund, so he should be available; Gladbach also hope to have captain Tim Kleindienst back from his muscle tear by then. Bremen's goals tend to come late, 14 of their 17 after half-time.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: Gladbach's league games have averaged over four goals (12 scored, 25 conceded) and Bremen's about 3.6, with Füllkrug scoring in seven straight games before the defeat at Stuttgart. Bremen's habit of scoring late adds to the case.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners. Bremen should have more of the ball, but Gladbach under Blessin defend with a back three and look to counter through Wael Mohya, which does not add corners on its own. I see nothing that moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean slightly higher: Bremen have taken three bookings in each of their last two games, and Gladbach's frustration has cost them yellows and a red recently. A bottom side chasing points away from home usually adds a couple of late cautions.

shots.text: The site has 31.6 shots, 18.6 for Bremen. Against a defence that has conceded 25, that home volume is reasonable, and Gladbach's 13 is fair if Kleindienst returns. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 on target, which is high. Bremen took 13 shots at Stuttgart without scoring and Gladbach have struggled to test keepers without Kleindienst, so I lean slightly lower even while expecting goals.
